lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: A two-game skid has exposed the Leafs' familiar soft underbelly: too much talent, not enough control when the game turns frantic. The latest blow came Wednesday, a 5-4 loss to Seattle, leaving Toronto 7-6, eighth in the Eastern Conference with 16 points - three behind the teams above them. Chris Tanev's expected return Saturday is the meaningful development: the 36-year-old defenceman practiced beside Morgan Rielly in Vancouver and said all signs point to playing after missing time with an upper-body injury. Dakota Joshua is also set to rejoin the lineup after missing the season to date, giving Toronto some overdue bite. Tanev's return will not cure the late-game leaks by itself, but it can steady a defence that has surrendered 10 goals across its last two defeats. Now comes Saturday's 7 p.m. visit to Vancouver - a chance to stop the slide before it becomes the season's defining habit.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: Toronto's offseason has begun with a small move that carries a larger message: roster space is now currency. Rudy Martin Jr. cleared waivers and was assigned to Triple-A Buffalo, opening a 40-man spot - a sensible, unsentimental decision for a club that finished 79-83, second in the AL East, and now needs more than cosmetic repair. The Jays must protect prospects before the Rule 5 deadline while seven players return from the 60-day injured list, making every slot matter. But the sharper issue is the lineup. Toronto needs power, and the proposed Marte trade deserves a serious hearing if it brings impact without gutting the farm system. Suzuki, meanwhile, belongs on the priority list only if the price matches the fit. Watch the next 40-man moves - and whether Ross Atkins turns cleared space into a genuine middle-of-the-order bat.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors left Friday night with a loss, but also with proof that Scottie Barnes can seize a game by the collar. Barnes scored a career-high 41 points in Toronto's 121-114 defeat against Orlando, shooting 19-for-34 before fouling out. That is star-level production - and it still wasn't enough. Toronto fell to 3-2, slipped to third in the Atlantic Division and carries a one-game losing streak into November. The larger concern is Kawhi Leonard, who remains out with swelling in his left knee; the Raptors have now lost twice in three games without him. Barnes can fill a scoring vacuum, but he cannot alone patch every defensive crack or close every late-game gap. Sunday's 9 p.m. visit to the Lakers is the next measuring stick - particularly whether Toronto's young core can turn Barnes' brilliance into a road win.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season's thin margin just got thinner. Daron Payne's significant foot injury, suffered in Friday's practice, has knocked Washington's anchor out of Sunday night's meeting with Philadelphia and may send him to injured reserve. That is a brutal blow for a 1-4-1 club already third in the NFC East, 2.5 games behind, and riding a one-game losing streak after the 23-17 defeat to San Francisco on Oct. 19. Payne had started all six games and recorded 14 tackles and a sack; now both starting defensive tackles could be sidelined against the Eagles. The timing is especially cruel for first-year coordinators still searching for their answers, and for a defense that cannot afford another collapse. At 8:20 p.m. Sunday on NBC, Washington must contain Philadelphia without Payne - and prove its season still has a pulse.

article.title: Tanev, Joshua Return for Leafs Against Canucks
paragraphs: The Leafs head to Vancouver tonight with Chris Tanev and Dakota Joshua set to return. Tanev last played October 10, while Joshua has not appeared this season. Anthony Stolarz starts against Kevin Lankinen at 7:00 PM ET on Sportsnet, with Toronto at 7-6 and eighth in the Eastern Conference.

The Jays are looking ahead after outfielder Rudy Martin Jr. cleared waivers, while Bo Bichette has opted in for another season with the Mets. The Raptors regroup after Scottie Barnes scored a career-high 41 points in Friday's 121-114 loss to Orlando. Jakob Poeltl had 11 rebounds and Immanuel Quickley eight assists; Toronto visits the Lakers Sunday at 9:00 PM ET.

The Commanders face the Eagles Sunday at 8:20 PM ET on NBC, but Daron Payne is out after suffering a significant foot injury in practice and could land on injured reserve. Washington enters at 1-4-1, third in the NFC East.
